comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme pages, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC joint degree with Leiden University centred on the living cell and on applying chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, bioinformatics and pharmacology to biotechnology and health. The official curriculum chart linked by the current programme page is dated September 2026. It accounts for the complete 180 EC and is reproduced below at its exact printed component-credit level; Dutch component titles are translated into English.

exception.reason: Life Science and Technology is an integrated biotechnology and bioprocess-engineering degree. Its compulsory spine combines molecular and cellular biology with bio-organic and chemical biology, molecular analytical methods, thermodynamics and transport phenomena, microbial physiology and biotechnology, genetic engineering, biocatalysis, bioinformatics, bioprocess modelling, basic biotechnology techniques, a microbial-biotechnology practicum, sustainable process design and a 20-EC final project. UCR offers meaningful molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology, genetics, pharmacology, laboratory, calculus, programming and data-science courses. It does not offer the required chemistry and bioprocess-engineering progression, including bio-organic and chemical biology, bioprocess thermodynamics, transport phenomena, microbial process engineering, biocatalysis, reactor/process modelling and sustainable biotechnological process design, nor an equivalent advanced biotechnology laboratory and capstone sequence. Combining UCR's strongest life-science, mathematics and computational courses would create a substantial molecular-biomedicine pathway, but not a defensible Life Science and Technology comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official September 2026 curriculum chart accounts for the full 180 EC: 60 EC in each year. Year one establishes molecular cell biology, biotechnology, immunology, biophysics, biochemistry, bioprocess thermodynamics, calculus, bio-organic chemistry, laboratory work, societal context, basic biotechnology techniques, programming and modelling. Year two advances immunology, chemical and structural biology, genetic engineering, calculus, microbial physiology, bioprocess modelling, biocatalysis, molecular analytical methods, microbial-biotechnology laboratory work, bioinformatics and transport phenomena. Year three comprises a genuine 30-EC minor, 5 EC on human disease processes, 5 EC on sustainable biotechnological process design and a 20-EC bachelor final project. The live programme page characterises the degree as a joint TU Delft–Leiden programme focused on understanding and influencing cellular processes and using microorganisms to design biotechnological processes for health, food, industry and the environment.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology and HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry provide strong foundations in cells, molecular mechanisms, biomolecules and metabolism. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory adds biochemical and molecular laboratory practice with bacteria, GMOs, protein production, DNA analysis and basic bioinformatics. HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology extend genetics, immunology, disease, drugs and physiology. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics and DISDATA211 Machine Learning support programming, modelling and quantitative analysis. The workbook nevertheless contains no organic-chemistry sequence, chemical-biology sequence, structural-biology course, dedicated molecular analytical chemistry, bioprocess thermodynamics, transport phenomena for biological systems, microbial-physiology sequence, industrial microbial biotechnology, biocatalysis, bioprocess or reactor modelling, biotechnology process-design studio, or advanced microbial-biotechnology practicum. HCBLIFE214 is a valuable single introductory laboratory course, but it cannot replace the target programme's staged biotechnology techniques and process laboratory formation. The available UCR courses also do not culminate in a 20-EC experimental or design project in biotechnology or bioprocess engineering. The closest UCR combination therefore covers biological and computational foundations while leaving the target's defining chemistry, engineering, process-design and advanced laboratory spine unmatched.
